title: Basil and Pine Nut Pesto
summary: Fresh basil blended with toasted pine nuts, garlic and olive oil, with grated Parmesan stirred through at the end.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast the pine nuts
steps.text: Toast the pine nuts in the dry pan over medium-low heat, stirring often, for 3-4 min until pale golden. Tip them onto a plate straight away so they stop cooking and cool.

steps.title: Make the paste
steps.text: Process the pine nuts and garlic until finely chopped. Add the basil and salt and pulse to a coarse green paste, scraping down the bowl between bursts.

steps.title: Stream in the oil
steps.text: With the motor running, pour the olive oil through the feed tube in a thin stream. Stop as soon as the pesto looks smooth and glossy; over-processing warms and darkens the basil.

steps.title: Stir in the cheese
steps.text: Scrape the pesto into a bowl and fold in the grated Parmesan by hand so it stays light rather than gluey.

steps.title: Use it
steps.text: Toss with freshly drained pasta, loosening with a spoonful of the starchy cooking water, or spoon over soups, new potatoes and sliced tomatoes.

tips: Make sure the basil leaves are completely dry so the pesto does not turn watery.
Never heat pesto in a pan; toss it with hot pasta off the heat to keep it green.
Walnuts or almonds can stand in for pine nuts if you prefer.
Top stored pesto with a thin layer of olive oil to stop the surface darkening.
storage: Keep in a jar under a film of olive oil in the fridge for up to 4 days. Freeze in small portions for up to 3 months. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
